arxiv-2106-01383.title: Discovery of a new nearby globular cluster with extreme kinematics located in the extension of a halo stream
arxiv-2106-01383.creator: Dante Minniti, José G. Fernández-Trincado, Matías Gómez, Leigh C. Smith, Philip W. Lucas, R. Contreras Ramos
arxiv-2106-01383.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Dante Minniti, José G. Fernández-Trincado, Matías Gómez, Leigh C. Smith, Philip W. Lucas, R. Contreras Ramos. We report the discovery of VVV-CL160, a new nearby globular cluster (GC) with extreme kinematics, located in the Galactic plane at l = 10.1477 l=10.1477 deg, b = 0.2999 b=0.2999 deg. We aim to characterize the physical properties of this new GC and place it in the context of the Milky Way, exploring its possible connection with the known GC NGC 6544 and with the Hrid halo stream.

arxiv-2106-05804.title: Topological energy release from collision of relativistic antiferromagnetic solitons
arxiv-2106-05804.creator: R. M. Otxoa, R. Rama-Eiroa, P. E. Roy, G. Tatara, O. Chubykalo-Fesenko, U. Atxitia
arxiv-2106-05804.description: Abstract Magnetic solitons offer functionalities as information carriers in multiple spintronic and magnonic applications. However, their potential for nanoscale energy transport has not been revealed. Here we demonstrate that antiferromagnetic solitons, e.g. domain walls, can uptake, transport and release energy.

arxiv-2201-12479.title: Total positivity and conjugacy classes
arxiv-2201-12479.creator: Xuhua He, George Lusztig
arxiv-2201-12479.description: Abstract . In this paper we study the interaction between the totally positive monoid G ⩾ 0 G_{\geqslant 0} attached to a connected reductive group G G with a pinning and the conjugacy classes in G G . In particular we study how a conjugacy class meets the various cells of G ⩾ 0 G_{\geqslant 0} .

arxiv-2203-06313.title: Performance Analysis of Intelligent Reflecting Surface Assisted Opportunistic Communications
arxiv-2203-06313.creator: L. Yashvanth, Chandra R. Murthy
arxiv-2203-06313.description: Abstract Intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRSs) are a promising technology for enhancing coverage and spectral efficiency, both in the sub-6 GHz and the millimeter wave (mmWave) bands. Existing approaches to leverage the benefits of IRS involve the use of a resource-intensive channel estimation step followed by a computationally expensive algorithm to optimize the reflection coefficients at the IRS.

arxiv-2302-11227.creator: Hao Wang, Yuan-Chuan Zou, Yu Liu
arxiv-2302-11227.description: Abstract Eccentricity has become an increasingly important parameter in gravitational wave studies as it can clearly reflect the dynamics of compact object mergers. Obtaining an accurate and fast gravitational waveform template is of paramount importance for accurately estimating gravitational wave parameters.

arxiv-2309-11255.title: On special quadratic Lyapunov functions for linear dynamical systems with an invariant cone
arxiv-2309-11255.creator: Omri Dalin, Alexander Ovseevich, Michael Margaliot
arxiv-2309-11255.description: Abstract We consider a continuous-time linear time-invariant dynamical system that admits an invariant cone. For the case of a self-dual and homogeneous cone we show that if the system is asymptotically stable then it admits a quadratic Lyapunov function with a special structure. The complexity of this Lyapuonv function scales linearly with the dimension of the dynamical system.

arxiv-2505-06437.creator: Shuo Ma †, Jonathan Dolde †, Xin Zheng †, Dhruva Ganapathy, Alexander Shtov, Jenny Chen, Anke Stöltzel, Shimon Kolkowitz

The pursuit of ever-longer optical coherence is central to advancing the precision of optical clocks. Synchronous differential clock comparisons have now demonstrated atomic coherence times on optical transitions that far exceed the coherence time of the clock laser.

arxiv-2509-22079.title: Multimodal Speckle-polarization Fiber-optic Sensing for Localized and High-bandwidth Vibration Monitoring
arxiv-2509-22079.creator: Catarina S. Monteiro, Tomás Lopes, Joana Teixeira, Tiago Ferreira, Pedro A. S. Jorge, Nuno A. Silva
arxiv-2509-22079.description: Abstract High-bandwidth and multi-point acoustic and vibration sensing is a critical asset for real-time condition monitoring, maintenance, and surveillance applications. In the case of large scales and harsh environments, optical fiber distributed sensing has emerged as a compelling alternative to electronic transducers, featuring lower installation and maintenance costs, along with compact footprints and enhanced robustness.

pmc-11507920.creator: Manuela Maria Iftime, Gabriela Liliana Ailiesei, Daniela Ailincai
pmc-11507920.description: Dynamic chitosan-based hydrogels with enhanced antioxidant activity were synthesized through the formation of reversible imine linkages with 5-methoxy-salicylaldehyde. pmc-11864722.title: Co-opted ATG2 lipid transfer protein delivers phospholipids for biogenesis of viral replication organelles
pmc-11864722.creator: Yuanrong Kang, Judit Pogany, Peter D Nagy
pmc-11864722.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Tomato bushy stunt virus (TBSV), an extensively-studied plant virus replicating in yeast model host and plants, hijacks ATG2 (autophagy-related 2), a lipid transfer protein (LTP) that transports lipids between adjacent organelles at membrane contact sites, for the biogenesis of their membranous VROs.

pmc-13324581.title: Artificial intelligence in chronic kidney disease: Early detection, risk prediction, and personalized treatment strategies
pmc-13324581.creator: Kirolos Eskandar
pmc-13324581.description: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a heterogeneous and frequently underdiagnosed condition in which conventional diagnostic and prognostic approaches based on static biomarkers and linear risk models offer limited sensitivity for early detection and individualized risk stratification. Artificial intelligence (AI) enables integration of longitudinal, high-dimensional, and multimodal clinical data, providing opportunities to address key limitations in current CKD care.

pmc-13330269.title: Use of multisensory information as facilitator of group schema therapy for borderline personality disorder
pmc-13330269.creator: Tarja Koffert, Sinikka Luutonen, Jarmo Hietala
pmc-13330269.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundGroup schema therapy (GST) has been found to be an effective form of treatment for borderline personality disorder (BPD) patients. Yet high drop-out rates and heterogenous treatment responses remain challenges in the real-life clinical care of BPD.MethodWe suggest a novel method for facilitating BPD group therapy using recordings (videos) made by patients at home according to the therapists’ instructions and watched together in the group session. Patient examines his/her observations on the video in the group under the guidance of psychotherapist.

pmc-13549708.title: Barriers to Treatment Resulting in Multiple Coexisting Infections and Hospice in a Young Person With Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS)
pmc-13549708.creator: Alexandra Bartholomew, Mason Calico, John Macaulay, Catherine Loehr, Shane Sanne
pmc-13549708.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Barriers to treatment in people with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) are often multifactorial and can lead to devastating outcomes. The authors present the case of a young woman with HIV who eventually developed acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) attributed to barriers to continuous treatment, including difficulty attending appointments, obstacles to obtaining medication, untreated depression, lack of a support system, and other unmet social needs. She unfortunately developed multiple complications related to her AIDS diagnosis, including numerous hospital admissions and several severe infections.
